problem.text: Attention previously invoked K and V projections separately. The change combines eligible EXL3 projections for small token batches, targeting greater GPU parallelism.

reasoning.text: The native edits are prerequisites for the attention call: the wrapper now accepts absent indices, and the kernel interprets them as sequential matrix selection rather than dereferencing a null pointer.

impact.text: Q remains separate. Unfused K/V execution remains available when fusion is unavailable or batch size times sequence length exceeds 32; this is not a threshold on the number of KV heads.

source_notes.text: The earlier routed-expert entry establishes MultiLinear's origin and its equal-dimension, equal-bitrate, bias-free, unscaled preconditions.

That entry's all-expert fused-buffer mismatch is carried over: routing can select num_experts while buffers still use num_experts_per_tok, and the native index-count check remains. Moving MultiLinear does not repair this conditional BlockSparseMLP failure.

Issue #16, “RuntimeError: CUDA error: invalid configuration argument,” concerns conversion and tokenizer truncation. Its relationship here is only inferred shared-source context: its traceback passes through project_qkv, specifically the unchanged Q projection, rather than the new fused K/V call.

limitations: No CUDA execution, numerical-equivalence test, or speed measurement was performed. The Python check models integer dispatch and shape arithmetic only.
The inspected source does not establish an empirical justification for the 32-token crossover.
Full compatibility of the new direct native call with every Linear instrumentation path and model-specific customization remains unestablished.

chapters.title: Parallel K/V projection through reusable multi-GEMM

claims.text: MultiLinear moves unchanged from block_sparse_mlp.py into its own module. It retains references to the linears and constructs device pointer tables for trellis weights and input/output transforms. Its constructor asserts uniform dimensions, bit width and experimental codebook multipliers, absent bias and softcap, and unit post-scale. Its unload method remains a no-op.

Attention.load attempts fusion when K and V are EXL3, have equal output widths and bit widths, and lack bias. MultiLinear then enforces its additional assertions. Attention initializes the helper to None and clears its reference during unload.

For m = batch size × query length at most 32, project_qkv views the shared input as [1,m,hidden_size], allocates separate transformed-input scratch [2,m,hidden_size] and FP16 output [2,m,num_kv_heads×head_dim], and calls exl3_mgemm without indices or routing weights. Output slices 0 and 1 become K and V with their original three-dimensional shapes.

The existing kernel broadcasts a single input matrix across projections but applies each projection's own input transform, trellis multiplication and output transform. Omitting weights leaves the output-transform normalization unchanged. The three attention consumers—SDPA, uncached FlashAttention and cached FlashAttention—continue reshaping K/V into heads before normalization, RoPE and attention.

Whole-tree search found the existing Python multi-GEMM calls only in BlockSparseMLP: gate and up broadcast an input with selected-expert indices; down consumes per-expert inputs and supplies routing weights. Those calls remain indexed and use a single-token guard. Attention instead explicitly constructs two output slots and permits up to 32 tokens; it supplies no expert-routing data.

The selector supports bit widths 1–8 and reduces the per-matrix grid using a tile-count heuristic divided by 12, marked experimentally chosen. The launcher then uses concurrency = min(total_sms / selected_sms, output_matrix_count). For K/V, this can schedule two matrix groups concurrently, but does not guarantee doubled parallelism.

A scalar transcription with 80 total SMs yielded concurrency two for a 20-SM per-matrix grid, but one for 50- or 80-SM grids. It also confirmed that both [1,32] and [2,16] token layouts meet the cutoff, whereas [1,33] does not.

The implementation supports the stated small-KV-head motivation: narrow projections can leave capacity for another matrix group. The tradeoff is additional two-projection scratch/output allocation and a specialized path instead of separate Linear.forward calls; actual benefit remains workload-dependent.

annotation.summary: Reuses multi-GEMM to combine eligible EXL3 K/V projections for at most 32 tokens, with sequential matrix selection and conditional two-matrix GPU concurrency.
